message.content:
Sure! Below is a quick “recipe” you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or adapt to your preferred language) to post the comment to VirusTotal.

---

## 1️⃣ Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X POST \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments" \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "type":"comment",
           "attributes":{
             "text":"Confirmed #malware"
           }
         }'
```

**What this does**

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `-X POST` | Sends a POST request |
| URL | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments` – the endpoint for adding a comment to the IP `192.168.1.1` |
| `-H "x-apikey: ABC321"` | Your API key (replace with your own if needed) |
| `-H "Content-Type: application/json"` | Tells VT that the body is JSON |
| `-d '{…}'` | The JSON payload you supplied |

> **Tip:** If you’re on Windows PowerShell, wrap the JSON in single quotes (`'…'`) or escape double quotes appropriately.

---

## 2️⃣ Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": "ABC321",
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
}
payload = {
    "type": "comment",
    "attributes": {
        "text": "Confirmed #malware"
    }
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())
```

---

### Things to keep in mind

| Item | Note |
|------|------|
| **Private IPs** | `192.168.1.1` is a private‑network address. VirusTotal typically only stores public IPs, so the API might return a *404 Not Found* or *400 Bad Request*. |
| **Rate limits** | VT enforces rate limits per API key. If you hit a limit, you’ll see a `429 Too Many Requests`. |
| **Error handling** | Always check `response.status_code`. A `200` or `201` means success; anything else indicates an error. |
| **Security** | Never expose your API key in public scripts or logs. Store it in environment variables or a secrets manager. |

---

Run one of the snippets above, and you should see a JSON response confirming that the comment was added (or an error message if something went wrong). Let me know if you hit any snags!
